thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: P50 latency and 5xx rates elevated on /v2/generate across us-west-2. Thresholds breached for 6m. Paging oncall.

jake_oncall: I'm on it. seeing surge in 504 and 502s from gateway. pulling up dashboards.

maria_sre: I'm seeing scheduler queue depth spike on batcher pods, head-of-line blocking on tenant-shared queue. KV cache miss ratio is low but memory for cache grew ~2.2x.

jake_oncall: @maria_sre can you paste the relevant query?

maria_sre: sure, from grafana: `sum(rate(gateway_5xx_count[1m])) by (route)` -> /v2/generate is the hot route.

maria_sre: also: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[2m])) by (le))` shows token-latency jump from 40ms to 280ms on backed batcher pods.

timothy_infra: looking at batcher logs: lots of long-running batches stuck waiting on KV cache fetch for very large sequences. snippet: ```
2024-04-05T13:21:09Z ERROR batcher/scheduler.go:245 waitForPrefix: timeout waiting for completion after 30s
2024-04-05T13:21:09Z WARN batcher/queue.go:512 head-of-line: batchID=blk-89 pending=72
```

jake_oncall: sounds like scheduler saturation causing gateway timeouts downstream. Impact: ~12% requests 5xx, several customers reporting timeouts. Clare, product/customer impact?

clare_product: we've got 3 customer support tickets and 1 enterprise alert. Latency is causing a degraded experience on two customers' flows (embedding-heavy). Tiered customers flagged.

ops_mike: quick mitigation idea: split hot route to overflow pool or route to a lighter quantized model variant. Can we flip routing rules?

maria_sre: we have a fallback variant available: model-quant-q4f. It's slightly lower quality but faster. Routing config is managed by the control-plane; I can stage a canary.

jake_oncall: do it. While staging, we should also relieve the scheduler: reduce max_batch_size and enable preemptive eviction for low-priority batches.

maria_sre: applying temporary scheduler params now: ```
PATCH /api/v1/scheduler/config
{
  "max_batch_size": 32,
  "eviction_policy": "low-priority-first",
  "queue_capacity": 120
}
```

maria_sre: pushed. Confirming rollout to batcher mgrs...

incident-bot: deploy-bot started rollout job scheduler-config-1723456789 by maria_sre.

deploy-bot: rollout 10% -> 100% over 2m. Logs: job succeeded.

maria_sre: scheduler params updated on all batchers. queue depth dropping slowly.

timothy_infra: in parallel, I enabled an overflow route: requests matching header X-Overflow: true -> model-quant-q4f in us-west-2. Command: `redwood route add --from /v2/generate --to model-quant-q4f --weight 0.3`

jake_oncall: good. also throttling background eval traffic that shares the same scheduler to free capacity.

ops_mike: observing gateway 5xx reduce to ~4% after route + scheduler patch. P95 latency down to ~120ms.

clare_product: flagging customers that we routed some traffic to fallback model with possible quality regressions. sending customer note now.

maria_sre: follow-up: noticed KV cache process on batcher-7 restarted twice in last 10m; investigating growth root cause. Might be a memory leak in cache sharding when seq_len > 2048.

timothy_infra: as longer-term fix we should cap max_seq_len for autosplit to 2048 and enable aggressive kv-ttl. I'll open an infra task but won't block live mitigation.

jake_oncall: next steps: 1) Keep overflow route for 30m, 2) leave reduced batch size for 15m, 3) collect perf/quality metrics and revert if errors drop below baseline, 4) create post-incident action items for cache patch.

maria_sre: capturing logs + grep for stuck batches: ```
kubectl logs batcher-7 | grep "head-of-line" -n | tail -n 50
```

maria_sre: grabbed batchIDs to evict low-priority ones manually: ```
POST /internal/batcher/evict
{"batch_ids": ["blk-89","blk-92","blk-101"]}
```

ops_mike: eviction accepted, queues trimmed.

incident-bot: PAGE ACK: jake_oncall acknowledged the page and marked incident as "mitigating".

clare_product: customers replied: two OK with degraded quality for short window, enterprise wants RCA.

jake_oncall: I'll keep monitoring for 30 minutes. If 5xx remains <2% and latency stable, we'll revert overflow routing and restore batch size.

maria_sre: note: we'll schedule a rollout to cap seq_len and a kv GC tuning next week. Creating ticket INFRA-824.

timothy_infra: adding logs/trace to correlate KV growth to specific prompt patterns.

jake_oncall: thanks all. Good mitigation — routing fallback + scheduler throttles did the trick. Postmortem to follow. :thumbsup:

ops_mike: logging incident timeline and actions to the incident doc now.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. If errors re-escalate, re-open page.
